name: Japan
notes: House of Representatives: 289 single-member constituencies (first-past-the-post) + 176 PR seats in 11 regional blocs (D'Hondt, no threshold). Baseline: the 8 February 2026 snap election (LDP 316 seats, a two-thirds majority). The district tier projects winners by plurality from the 2026 top-two baselines (winner + runner-up shares from the results article - no full candidate lists); its swing is anchored on the national PR baseline, the same measure as the party-support polls (feeding the PR shares reproduces all 289 baseline winners). The PR tier uses per-bloc D'Hondt with a uniform swing from the same baseline; the real allocation also reallocates seats forfeited by list exhaustion (not modelled) and the official per-party PR totals are 67/42/20/16/15/11/4/1. Polls: the raw party-support shares (including 'no party') are used as vote proxies - they track actual vote shares closely (pre-election polls showed LDP ~40 against the 36.72 actual), so no undecided redistribution is applied. Party names follow the 2026 realignment: the Centrist Reform Alliance became the Centrist Reform Party (CRP) and Reiwa Shinsengumi became the Party of Life. Geometry: the Commons 2024 constituency map (data-name labels; Akita unlabeled and Wakayama-2 typo handled; 2022 reapportionment cuts included). Next election: by February 2030.
